title: Variable-span clusterizer and pad-pruner scheduler for sequence-aware shaping
creator: Ariana Chen
description: Problem: large variance in request sequence length causes significant padding waste when coalescing into GPU batches. Current fixed-bucket schemes create high tail cost for mixed workloads (chat + short queries). Goal: implement a runtime component that clusters requests by variable sequence-span affinity, prunes pad tokens via aggressive alignment heuristics at prefill time, and co-schedules prefill + decode to enable kernel selection that minimizes padded tokens and maximizes kernel efficiency. This ticket scopes the algorithm, a reference prototype in the runtime, metrics, and an A/B experiment on a subset of customer traffic.
technical_design: High-level approach: compute a lightweight fingerprint (span-hash) per request based on token-length, prefix-presence, and client-declared intent; group compatible spans into dynamic clusters where span width is adaptive rather than fixed-size buckets; within each cluster run a pad-prune pass that: (1) orders sequences to maximize common-prefix coalescing, (2) trims trailing pad regions detectable at prefill using model EOS heuristics, and (3) marks sequences for split-decode if kernel affinity suggests interleaving yields higher throughput.

Dataflow changes: add Clusterizer stage between request-queue and packer; stage emits cluster_id and cluster_metadata (max_seq, median_seq, kernel_hint). Clusterizer is probabilistic and has a tunable aggressiveness parameter to trade padding savings vs scheduling overhead.

Kernel selection integration: use cluster_metadata to prefer kernels with good small-seq throughput (fused-attention variants) or long-seq streaming kernels; expose kernel_hint to the runtime's kernel-selector so it can pin cluster shards to a compatible GPU kernel variant.

Attention optimizations: inside pad-prune pass, apply a grouped-KV compacting transform for requests with identical encoder prefix hashes to reduce KV cache footprint; enable sparse-attention fallback only when cluster density and sequence length exceed thresholds.

Prefill/Decode co-scheduling: implement a two-phase scheduler that attempts to align prefill batches that create high prefix overlap with upcoming decode requests, allowing reuse of warmed KV cache and lowering first-token latency for decodes that immediately follow prefill-heavy requests.

Metrics and telemetry: collect padded_tokens_saved, pad_overhead_ratio, cluster_surface_area, kernel_switch_rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies for prefill and decode, and cost-per-1k-tokens estimate. Emit histograms keyed by cluster_id and model_variants.
Feature flags: runtime.feature.clusterizer_enabled, runtime.feature.pad_pruner_aggressiveness (0..100), runtime.feature.kernel_hinting. All flags default to off for safety and require rollout guard.
Fallbacks and safety: if pad-prune increases latency beyond threshold or affects correctness (detected via evals), disable for the offending cluster and roll back via guardrail automation.
Compatibility: maintain compatibility with Dedicated and Private by making clusterizer a modular plugin that can be enabled per-deployment with resource-aware defaults.
Storage/State: clusterizer maintains only ephemeral in-memory counters and sliding-window histograms per model-shard; no persistent state required.

Performance targets: reduce average padded tokens per batch by >= 20% on mixed-length production traces; keep p99 decode latency within +5% of baseline; reduce per-token compute cost by >= 7% on experimental traffic.

Open questions: (1) How to safely detect model-generated EOS without full decode? (2) What aggressiveness defaults should we use for short-lived bursty traffic? (3) Should cluster_ids be sticky per-client session for better KV reuse?
acceptance_criteria: Prototype integrated into the runtime on staging and can be toggled with feature flags
Telemetry shows pad_overhead_ratio drop >= 20% on the mixed-workload test corpus compared to baseline
No increase in error rates or incorrect model outputs attributable to pad pruning (evaluated by automated regression prompts)
p99 decode latency increase <= 5% and p50 improved for prefill-aligned decodes
Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and infra leads
Automated rollback triggers implemented for latency or correctness regressions

risks: Pad pruning could accidentally trim tokens that change model semantics if EOS heuristics are too aggressive
Extra scheduler complexity may increase head latency for some traffic shapes
Kernel_hint churning might reduce cache locality if cluster_ids are not stable
Feature interactions with Dedicated autoscaler could cause unexpected daily throughput cliffs
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal canary on non-critical workloads (0.5%) with detailed telemetry
Beta: 5% customer traffic for 72 hours with automatic rollback triggers
Gradual ramp: 20% for 24 hours, then 50% if metrics stable, then full rollout per region
Dedicated/private: manual opt-in with low-aggressiveness defaults and customer-facing notes
Post-rollout: run quality evals and k-anomaly detection for 7 days
timeline: Week 1: finalize design and prototype APIs
Week 2: full prototype + internal perf runs
Week 4: analysis and beta ramp decision
experiment_results: Staging run (mixed chat+short queries) showed padded_tokens_saved = 24% and pad_overhead_ratio down from 1.44 to 1.10
p50 decode latency improved by ~6ms for prefill-aligned requests; p99 went up by 3% in initial prototype due to scheduling overhead (investigating)
Kernel switch rate rose by 8% but overall GPU util improved slightly due to denser small-seq kernel packing
